nodes.content: Infer calibrated cell ancestry from incomplete lineage barcodes and transcriptional states despite state convergence and biased lineage sampling.
requirements: Improve ancestral-pair AUROC by ≥0.05 over barcode-only inference with 30% barcode dropout.
Achieve ancestry-probability expected calibration error ≤0.05 under convergent states and uneven lineage sampling.

nodes.content: Develop a dropout-aware Bayesian lineage model combining barcode likelihoods, convergent-state transition mixtures, clone-sampling propensity correction, and held-out isotonic calibration.
How can shared transcriptional states be distinguished from common ancestry when barcode dropout and clone sampling bias distort evidence?
State-transition mixtures and sampling correction distinguish convergence, yielding ≥0.05 ancestral-pair AUROC gain over barcode-only and ECE ≤0.05 at 30% dropout.
Simulate convergent-state trees with 30% barcode dropout and biased sampling; fit propensity-corrected mixtures, calibrate probabilities, compare AUROC/ECE against barcode-only.
Benchmark calibrated mixtures against barcode-only on ConvergeTree-30 (100 convergent trees; 30% dropout; 4:1 sampling), measuring AUROC and ECE.
On ConvergeTree-30, ancestral-pair AUROC rose from 0.72 to 0.79 versus barcode-only, with ancestry-probability ECE 0.038.
Select the calibrated mixture for biological-lineage validation because ConvergeTree-30 meets both AUROC-gain and ECE thresholds.
ConvergeTree-30 benchmark report archives per-tree ancestral-pair AUROC, ancestry-probability reliability plots, sampling-stratum ECE, and reproducible simulation seeds.
Re-run the selected calibrated mixture on held-out ConvergeTree-30 seeds, auditing the benchmark report’s per-tree AUROC and sampling-stratum ECE.
Held-out ConvergeTree-30: ancestral-pair AUROC 0.77 versus 0.71 barcode-only; ECE 0.042 overall, ≤0.049 across sampling strata.
Mutation-consistency gating should reduce convergent-state false ancestry calls ≥20% while preserving undersampled-clone AUROC ≥0.75.
Using ConvergeTree-30 report seeds and per-tree AUROC, benchmark mutation-consistency gating against ungated mixtures on convergent-state false calls and undersampled-clone AUROC.
On ConvergeTree-30, gating reduced convergent-state false ancestry calls 23%, but undersampled-clone AUROC dropped from 0.76 to 0.72.
Retain ungated calibrated mixture: held-out metrics meet targets, while mutation-consistency gating harms undersampled-clone AUROC.
Develop mutation-anchored temporal optimal transport across transcriptional states, correcting clone abundance and calibrating ancestry probabilities by sampling stratum.
Fit time-resolved mutation-anchored transport, reweight clone sampling, and calibrate on held-out convergent lineages before evaluating AUROC/ECE at 30% dropout.
Using ConvergeTree-30 report seeds, generate timed cell cohorts and fit clone-reweighted, mutation-anchored transport at 30% dropout.
Timed ConvergeTree-30 transport bundle contains cohort timestamps, mutation-anchor masks, clone weights, ancestry scores, and held-out calibration splits.
Do temporal mutation anchors resolve convergent-state ancestry without miscalibrating probabilities for sparsely sampled clones?
Temporal anchors should raise ancestral-pair AUROC ≥0.05 over barcode-only while clone-stratified calibration keeps ECE ≤0.05 under 30% dropout.
Audit transport-bundle anchor masks and benchmark held-out ancestry scores against barcode-only, measuring AUROC, clone-stratified ECE, and anchor-ablation effects.
Timed ConvergeTree-30: transport AUROC reached 0.78 versus 0.71 barcode-only and 0.74 without anchors; worst clone-stratum ECE was 0.046.
Advance anchored transport to robustness testing because its 0.07 AUROC gain and worst-stratum ECE 0.046 satisfy targets.
Stress-test anchored transport versus the ungated calibrated mixture across 20–50% dropout and 2:1–10:1 clone imbalance, recording AUROC and ECE.
At 30% dropout and 10:1 imbalance, barcode-only AUROC was 0.70; mixture AUROC/ECE reached 0.76/0.048, versus transport’s 0.78/0.083.
Can stronger clone-abundance correction reduce transport ECE from 0.083 below 0.05 at 10:1 imbalance without sacrificing AUROC?
Fit clipped inverse-inclusion weights and clone-stratified temperature scaling on validation splits; retest held-out 10:1, 30%-dropout transport AUROC/ECE.
At 10:1 imbalance and 30% dropout, corrected transport reached AUROC 0.77 versus barcode-only 0.70, but ECE remained 0.061.
Use anchor-coverage-gated fusion of Bayesian lineage probabilities and temporal transport, with hierarchical clone-stratum calibration to withstand sampling imbalance.
Anchor coverage separates reliable transport predictions (ECE ≤0.05) from unreliable ones (ECE ≥0.08) at 10:1 imbalance, enabling gated fusion.
Can pairwise mutation-anchor coverage distinguish calibrated from miscalibrated transport ancestry probabilities under 10:1 clone imbalance?
Stratify held-out ConvergeTree-30 pairs by ≥2 versus <2 observed mutation anchors; compare transport ECE at 10:1 clone imbalance.
At 10:1 imbalance, transport ECE was 0.069 with ≥2 anchors and 0.094 with <2; high coverage missed 0.05.
Cross-tabulate anchor coverage with estimated clone-inclusion propensity; test whether propensity-matched high-coverage pairs achieve ECE ≤0.05 at 10:1 imbalance.
After propensity matching at 10:1 imbalance, transport ECE was 0.043 for ≥2-anchor pairs versus 0.089 for <2-anchor pairs.
Can propensity-matched anchor gating fuse transport’s AUROC advantage with the mixture’s calibration at 10:1 clone imbalance?
Train propensity-matched ≥2-anchor transport gate with mixture fallback and hierarchical calibration; compare held-out 10:1 AUROC/ECE against both components.
At 10:1 imbalance and 30% dropout, fusion AUROC/ECE was 0.79/0.044 versus mixture 0.76/0.048 and transport 0.78/0.083.
Select propensity-matched anchor gating for external validation: unadjusted high coverage miscalibrated, whereas matched fusion achieved AUROC 0.79 and ECE 0.044.
Train a clone-balanced contrastive ancestry encoder using time-ordered lineage positives, convergent-state hard negatives, dropout augmentation, and sampling-stratified calibration.
Can convergent-state hard negatives improve ancestry ranking without embedding clone-sampling frequencies that destabilize calibration under 10:1 imbalance?
Clone-balanced hard negatives improve AUROC ≥0.03 versus random negatives, while sampling-stratified calibration keeps ECE ≤0.05 at 10:1 imbalance.
Train hard-negative and random-negative encoders on ConvergeTree-30; calibrate by sampling stratum; compare AUROC/ECE at 10:1 imbalance.
Train clone-balanced hard-negative and random-negative encoders; compare held-out ConvergeTree-30 AUROC and sampling-stratified ECE at 10:1 imbalance.
ContrastiveBench-10 bundle stores matched encoder checkpoints, convergent-state negative-pair indices, clone sampling weights, held-out scores, and calibration splits.
Audit ContrastiveBench-10 negatives and calibration splits; compare hard- versus random-negative AUROC/ECE at 10:1 imbalance and 30% dropout.
ContrastiveBench-10: hard-negative AUROC 0.80 versus random-negative 0.76; worst sampling-stratum ECE was 0.047 at 30% dropout.
Advance hard-negative encoder alongside gated fusion: AUROC 0.80 and worst-stratum ECE 0.047 outperform ungated mixture without transport’s miscalibration.
